mainTopic: Where the כיור and מזבח stood, and the law of a damaged מזבח
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי הגלילי says only the מזבח stands at the entrance of the אהל מועד. He places the כיור between the אולם and the מזבח, pulled off to the south. The גמרא tests several views of where the מזבח stood and asks each time why the כיור was not placed directly between them, clear of the doorway. It concludes that he holds the whole מזבח was in the north, and that the word 'צפונה' keeps the north empty of vessels. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees: for him the north must be empty even of the מזבח. Next, רב rules that קרבנות slaughtered while the מזבח is damaged are פסול, and his forgotten source is found in 'וזבחת עליו'. רבי יוחנן disqualifies even living animals, and the two argue about whether בעלי חיים נדחים. The גמרא then defends רב against a ברייתא and against his own ruling about incense, explaining that blood needs a real מזבח. The amud ends with רבי יהודה's view that שלמה made the courtyard holy, and רבי יוסי's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the altar stands at the entrance, not the Basin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the end of the פסוק to mean that the מזבח stands at the entrance of the אהל מועד, but the כיור does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: “The altar of the burnt offering, etc.” This teaches that the altar is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, but the Basin is not at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes quoting a פסוק and learns from it that only the מזבח, not the כיור, may stand directly at the entrance of the אהל מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places the מזבח right at the entrance of the אהל מועד. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads this as a rule about the doorway: the כיור may not stand in that spot. This creates a puzzle, because another פסוק says the כיור stands 'between the אהל מועד and the מזבח.'

keyTerms.meaning: The altar of the burnt offering (the outer altar)
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting (in the בית המקדש, this matches the היכל)
The Basin that the כהנים washed their hands and feet from

phrases.english: “The altar of the burnt offering, etc.” —
phrases.notes: This is the end of a quoted פסוק: שמות 40:29.

phrases.english: the altar is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
but the Basin is not at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזבח stands at the entrance of the אהל מועד. The כיור may not stand in that spot.

steps.title: The Basin stood between the Entrance Hall and the altar, slightly south
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the כיור stood between the אולם and the מזבח, moved slightly toward the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where would he place the Basin? Between the Entrance Hall and the altar, pulled slightly toward the south.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us exactly where the כיור went. It stood between the אולם and the מזבח, shifted a little to the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כיור stands in the area between the אולם and the מזבח, but it is pulled south, off to the side of the מזבח, so it does not stand right between the מזבח and the doorway. The גמרא will next ask why רבי יוסי הגלילי did not simply place it directly between them, just outside the doorway's path.

keyTerms.meaning: The Entrance Hall at the front of the היכל

phrases.english: Where would he place it?
Between the Entrance Hall and the altar,
pulled slightly toward the south.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the כיור stands between the אולם and the מזבח, but moved slightly south so it is not right in front of the doorway.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 1 to give the actual location of the כיור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כיור is placed between the אולם and the מזבח, shifted slightly to the south.

steps.title: What does he hold about the altar's position?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what view of the מזבח's location lies behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's placement of the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what רבי יוסי הגלילי must believe about where the מזבח stands, since that decides where the כיור can go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the כיור can stand depends on where the מזבח stands, because the כיור must be between the building and the מזבח. The גמרא will now test several possible views and challenge each one.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold? (what view is behind his ruling)

phrases.english: What does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the placement given in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What position of the מזבח (north, south, or split) does רבי יוסי הגלילי assume?

steps.title: If the whole altar is in the south, the Basin could stand directly between
steps.stepSummary: If the entire מזבח is in the south, the כיור could stand from the line of the היכל wall and southward, directly between the אולם and the מזבח and still clear of the doorway. So why did רבי יוסי הגלילי push it off to the south side?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds that the entire altar stands in the south, let him place the Basin from the wall of the Sanctuary and southward, between the Entrance Hall and the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the whole מזבח is in the southern half. It challenges it: in that case there would be room to put the כיור fully south of the doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח were entirely in the south, the space between the building and the מזבח would stretch well south of the היכל doorway. The כיור could then be placed past the line of the היכל wall, out of the doorway's path, and still stand directly between the אולם and the מזבח. That would fit both פסוקים, so why move it off to the side?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him stand it (let him place it)

phrases.english: If he holds that the entire altar
stands in the south —
let him stand it from the wall of the Sanctuary and southward,
between the Entrance Hall and the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קָסָבַר כּוּלֵּיהּ מִזְבֵּחַ בְּדָרוֹם קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the whole מזבח is in the south.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were so, the כיור could stand directly between the אולם and the מזבח, south of the doorway line, so there would be no reason to push it off to the south side.

steps.title: Even if the Sanctuary and Entrance Hall share one holiness, there is still room
steps.stepSummary: Even if the היכל and אולם count as one level of holiness, so the כיור must also avoid the אולם doorway, it could still be placed from the אולם wall southward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he holds that the sanctity of the Sanctuary and the Entrance Hall is one, let him place the Basin from the wall of the Entrance Hall and southward, between the Entrance Hall and the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds to its challenge against the 'whole מזבח in the south' view. Even with a stricter assumption about the אולם, there would still be room further south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might defend the view by saying the אולם counts like the היכל, so the כיור must also stay clear of the wider אולם doorway. The גמרא answers that even then, with the whole מזבח in the south, the כיור could stand past the line of the אולם wall. It would still be directly between the אולם and the מזבח, so there is still no reason to push it off to the side.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the Sanctuary and the Entrance Hall

phrases.english: And even if he holds
that the sanctity of the Sanctuary and the Entrance Hall is one —
let him stand it from the wall of the Entrance Hall and southward,
in between the Entrance Hall and the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי קָסָבַר קְדוּשַּׁת הֵיכָל וְאוּלָם חֲדָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge in step 4 by blocking a possible defense.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of the 'whole מזבח in the south' view, based on treating the היכל and אולם as one level of holiness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even when the כיור must also avoid the אולם doorway, a southern מזבח would leave room past the אולם wall. So the 'slightly' placement still does not fit.

steps.title: If the altar is half north and half south, the Basin could still go further south
steps.stepSummary: If the מזבח is half in the north and half in the south, the כיור could still be placed from the line of the היכל wall and southward, between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, if he holds that half of the altar is in the north and half in the south, let him place the Basin from the wall of the Sanctuary and southward, between the Entrance Hall and the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a second possibility, that the מזבח is split down the middle between north and south. It challenges this view the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with the מזבח centered, it stretches out to the sides, beyond both edges of the היכל doorway. So the כיור could stand south of the היכל wall line, still in front of part of the מזבח, without blocking the doorway. So again, why did רבי יוסי הגלילי push it off to the side? Step 8 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of it in the north and half of it in the south

phrases.english: Alternatively, if he holds
that half of the altar is in the north and half in the south —
let him stand it from the wall of the Sanctuary and southward,
between the Entrance Hall and the altar!

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'from the wall of the היכל' as 'touching the wall.' It marks a north–south line: the כיור goes south of where that wall begins, so it is out of the doorway's path.
steps.whyThisMatters: By ruling out these possibilities, the גמרא is narrowing down what רבי יוסי הגלילי must hold about the מזבח's location. That question matters for where the מזבח stood in the עזרה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי קָסָבַר חֶצְיוֹ בַּצָּפוֹן וְחֶצְיוֹ בַּדָּרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a second possible answer to the question in step 3 and challenges it with the same reasoning used in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the מזבח is half in the north and half in the south.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A centered מזבח still extends past the doorway on both sides, leaving room to place the כיור directly between the אולם and the מזבח, south of the היכל wall line. So there is no reason to push it off to the side under this view either.

steps.title: The half-north view still fails, even if the אולם is as holy as the היכל
steps.stepSummary: Even if the מזבח is half north and half south, and the אולם counts as holy as the היכל, the כיור could stand from the אולם wall southward, directly between the אולם and the מזבח. So why push it off to the side?
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if he holds that the holiness of the אולם and the היכל is one and the same, let him place the כיור from the אולם wall and southward, between the אולם and the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps attacking the 'half north, half south' view of the מזבח. It uses the same move it used in step 5 against the 'all in the south' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the גמרא said that under the half-north view, the כיור could stand from the היכל wall southward. Here it adds that even if we must also keep clear of the אולם doorway, there is still room from the אולם wall southward, directly between the אולם and the מזבח. Either way, this view does not explain why the כיור was pushed off to the side.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of the אולם and the היכל is one level
The wall of the Entrance Hall

phrases.english: And even if he holds
that the holiness of the Entrance Hall and the Sanctuary is one,
let him place it from the wall of the Entrance Hall and southward,
between the Entrance Hall and the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי קָסָבַר קְדוּשַּׁת הָאוּלָם וְהֵיכָל חֲדָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 6 against the half-north view, the same way step 5 strengthened step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the מזבח was half north and half south
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view there would be room for the כיור directly between the אולם and the מזבח, south of the אולם doorway, so it would not need to be pushed off to the side.

steps.title: So רבי יוסי הגלילי must hold the whole מזבח was in the north
steps.stepSummary: Since the other two views don't fit, the גמרא concludes that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the entire מזבח stood in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not because he holds that the entire מזבח was in the north?
steps.whatsHappening: Both other options have failed, so the גמרא answers the question from step 3: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the whole מזבח was in the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מזבח is all in the north, the whole area directly between the אולם and the מזבח is either in front of the doorway or in the north. So south of the doorway there is no spot that is directly between them, and the כיור ends up off to the south side. The question is phrased as 'is it not?', but it works as the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (introduces the remaining explanation)
The entire מזבח is in the north

steps.confusionAlert: Even though it ends with a question mark, this line is not a new question. It is the גמרא's answer, phrased as 'isn't it obvious that...?'

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because
he holds that the entire altar is in the north?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both other views are ruled out in steps 4–7, this gives the only remaining view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which view of the מזבח's location lies behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's placement of the כיור (step 3)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He holds the entire מזבח was in the north.

steps.title: Even with the מזבח in the north, the כיור could go northward
steps.stepSummary: Even if the מזבח is entirely in the north, the כיור could stand from the היכל wall northward and still be between the אולם and the מזבח. Why move it south?
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you place it from the היכל wall and northward, it is still between the אולם and the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges its own new answer. Even with the whole מזבח in the north, there seems to be another place for the כיור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the מזבח in the north, the space north of the היכל doorway line is still between the אולם and the מזבח. Placing the כיור there avoids blocking the doorway. So why does רבי יוסי הגלילי shift it south at all?

phrases.english: Even if you place it
from the wall of the Sanctuary and northward,
it is still between the Entrance Hall and the altar;

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָמֵי מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ מִכּוֹתֶל הֵיכָל וְלַצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 8 by finding another place for the כיור under that view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'all in the north' view explains why the כיור is moved slightly south
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is open space to the north that is still between the אולם and the מזבח, so the כיור need not go south.

steps.title: Even keeping clear of the אולם doorway, the north still works
steps.stepSummary: Even if the אולם is as holy as the היכל, the כיור could stand from the אולם wall northward, still between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let him place it from the אולם wall and northward, between the אולם and the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes its challenge further, using the same pattern as steps 5 and 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the כיור must also keep clear of the wider אולם doorway, it could stand north of the אולם wall line. That spot is still between the אולם and the מזבח. So the challenge stands under either view of the אולם's holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: In the space between the אולם and the מזבח

phrases.english: And let him place it from the wall of the Entrance Hall and northward,
in the space between the Entrance Hall and the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 9's challenge to the case where the אולם is as holy as the היכל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'all in the north' explanation of 'slightly south'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with the stricter limit of keeping clear of the אולם doorway, there is still room on the north side.

steps.title: The פסוק 'צפונה' keeps the north empty of vessels
steps.stepSummary: The word 'צפונה' teaches that the north area must stay empty of vessels. So the כיור cannot stand on the north side and must shift slightly south.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'צפונה' (northward): this teaches that the north must be empty of vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of steps 9–10 with a פסוק. The north area must stay clear of vessels, so the כיור cannot be placed there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Space toward the north is not allowed, because 'צפונה' teaches that the north must be free of vessels. The כיור also cannot block the doorway. So the only option is to move it slightly south, exactly as רבי יוסי הגלילי said. This confirms that he holds the whole מזבח was in the north.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the whole מזבח was in the north. The כיור stands between the אולם and the מזבח but is moved slightly south, because it may not block the doorway and the north must stay empty of vessels.

phrases.english: The verse states: "northward" —
that the north should be empty of vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 9 and 10 by ruling out the north side for the כיור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that adds a new limit on where vessels may stand
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כיור could be placed toward the north, between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The north must be empty of vessels, so the כיור must move slightly south. This supports the view that the whole מזבח was in the north.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling, 'slightly south', fits only the view that the entire מזבח was in the north, together with the rule that the north stays empty of vessels.

steps.title: Who disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא argues with רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds the entire מזבח stood in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא that disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just concluded that רבי יוסי הגלילי puts the whole מזבח in the north. Now it asks who holds the opposite view, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא worked through several possible layouts of the מזבח. Once רבי יוסי הגלילי's view was pinned down, it wants to know which named תנא takes the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: Who is the תנא
who disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי?
phrases.notes: This is the view from Step 8, that the whole מזבח stood in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion about רבי יוסי הגלילי's position.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who argues with רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the north must be empty, even of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He learns from the word 'צפונה' that the north must be empty of everything, even the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. A ברייתא teaches that he says: 'צפונה' means the north must be empty of everything, even of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the one who disagrees. It quotes a ברייתא to show his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, 'צפונה' taught that the north must be free of vessels like the כיור. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב takes the same word further: even the מזבח may not stand in the north. So for him the whole מזבח is in the south, the opposite of רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: Northward, the word in the פסוק about where קרבנות are slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the whole מזבח was in the north. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the north must be totally empty, so the מזבח was in the south.

phrases.english: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:
'Northward': that the north should be empty of anything,
and even of the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who learns from 'צפונה' that the north must be empty even of the מזבח.

steps.title: רב: offerings slaughtered at a damaged altar are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if the מזבח is damaged, all קדשים slaughtered there are פסול. He says there is a פסוק for this, but he forgot it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: if the מזבח is damaged, all קדשים slaughtered there are פסול. We have a פסוק for this, but we forgot it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a ruling about a damaged מזבח and admits he cannot remember its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is that a קרבן slaughtered while the מזבח is damaged becomes פסול. רב is sure the rule comes from a פסוק, which opens the search for it in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav said: an altar that was damaged,
all the offerings slaughtered there are disqualified.
We have a verse for it, but we forgot it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים slaughtered while the מזבח is damaged are פסול.

steps.title: רב כהנא hears the question asked in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: When רב כהנא went up to ארץ ישראל, he heard רבי שמעון ברבי ask, in the name of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, where we learn that קדשים slaughtered at a damaged מזבח are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב כהנא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי שמעון the son of רבי saying in the name of רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי: from where do we know that if the מזבח is damaged, all קדשים slaughtered there are פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story that sets up the source for רב's rule. Someone in ארץ ישראל asks the exact question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question repeats רב's ruling word for word. That shows the sages of ארץ ישראל held the same law and knew its פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: When Rav Kahana went up,
he found Rabbi Shimon the son of Rabbi

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: saying in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:
From where do we know, regarding an altar that was damaged,
that all the offerings slaughtered there are disqualified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins finding the forgotten source for רב's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that a damaged מזבח makes slaughtered קדשים פסול.

steps.title: The verse: slaughter 'upon it' means only when the altar is whole
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'וזבחת עליו', 'you shall slaughter upon it'. Since we do not actually slaughter on top of the מזבח, it must mean slaughtering is allowed only when the מזבח is whole (שלם), not when it is lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And you shall slaughter upon it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings.' But do you really slaughter on top of it? Rather, it means: when it is whole, and not when it is lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The source is given. The word 'עליו' cannot be meant literally, so it is read as 'because of it', meaning the slaughter depends on the מזבח being whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals are slaughtered on the ground near the מזבח, not on top of it. So 'עליו' must teach something else: slaughter is valid only while the מזבח is whole. The word 'שלמיך' also hints at 'שלם', whole.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall slaughter upon it
Your peace offerings, which hints at שָׁלֵם

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying animals were slaughtered on the מזבח. It asks 'do you really slaughter on it?' to show the word 'עליו' must teach a different lesson.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And you shall slaughter upon it
your burnt offerings and your peace offerings'
But do you slaughter on it?!
Rather, when it is whole,
phrases.notes: Here 'it' means the מזבח. The word 'שלמיך' is being read like 'שלם', whole.

phrases.english: and not when it is lacking.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְזָבַחְתָּ עָלָיו אֶת עֹלֹתֶיךָ וְאֶת שְׁלָמֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'מנין' question with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that קדשים slaughtered at a damaged מזבח are פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 20:21, 'וזבחת עליו', read as 'when it is שלם'.

steps.title: This is the verse רב forgot
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא realizes that this is the פסוק רב could not remember.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: this is the verse that slipped away from רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא connects what he heard back to his teacher. The missing source for רב's rule has been found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the loop that Step 14 opened. רב's ruling now has a clear source in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Slipped away from him, he forgot it

steps.whatToRemember: רב: קדשים slaughtered while the מזבח is damaged are פסול, from 'וזבחת עליו', meaning only when the מזבח is שלם.

phrases.english: He said: this is the verse
that slipped away from Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the derivation back to רב's forgotten פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source for רב's rule is 'וזבחת עליו'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both kinds are disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says both kinds of animals are פסול: those already slaughtered and those not yet slaughtered while the מזבח was damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: both this one and that one are פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a stricter view than רב. Even animals that were not yet slaughtered when the מזבח was damaged become פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב only disqualified animals that were already slaughtered. רבי יוחנן adds the living animals that were set aside as קדשים while the מזבח was damaged.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both this and that are disqualified.
phrases.notes: He means both the slaughtered animals and the ones still alive when the מזבח was damaged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה פְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter view that argues with רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both slaughtered and not-yet-slaughtered קדשים are פסול when the מזבח is damaged.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רב and רבי יוחנן argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that slaughtered animals are פסול. The question is why רבי יוחנן also disqualifies the living ones and רב does not.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the dispute in Steps 14 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle of the רב and רבי יוחנן dispute.

steps.title: Can living animals be permanently pushed off?
steps.stepSummary: רב holds living animals are not permanently pushed off (בעלי חיים אינן נדחים). רבי יוחנן holds they are (בעלי חיים נדחים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds that living animals are not pushed off. רבי יוחנן holds that living animals are pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the argument. It depends on whether a living קרבן that becomes unusable for a while is pushed off forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, a living animal waits until the מזבח is fixed and can then be brought, so only slaughtered ones are lost. For רבי יוחנן, once the animal was pushed off while alive, it stays פסול forever, even after the מזבח is repaired.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: only slaughtered animals are פסול, because בעלי חיים אינן נדחים. רבי יוחנן: even living animals are פסול, because בעלי חיים נדחים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of דחוי, a קרבן being pushed off permanently, comes up in many places across קדשים. This sugya ties it to living animals.

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָבַר: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִדְחִים,
phrases.english: Rav holds: living animals are not pushed off,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִידְחִין.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan holds: living animals are pushed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָבַר: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִדְחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether living animals can be permanently pushed off (בעלי חיים נדחים).

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to contradict רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: sacrifices that existed before the מזבח was built are פסולין even after it is built.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: all sacrificial animals that existed before the altar was built, and then the altar was built, are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב. This step only sets up the source; the next lines will work out what it really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says living animals are not permanently pushed off. The ברייתא says animals that waited for a missing מזבח are פסולין, which sounds like living animals are pushed off. The גמרא now has to figure out what case the ברייתא is describing.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals, things set aside as holy

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
All sacrificial animals that were [set aside]
before the altar was built,
and afterward the altar was built, are disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's side of the argument just defined in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that living animals are not permanently pushed off (בעלי חיים אינן נדחים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules that animals waiting for a missing מזבח are פסולין, which implies living animals can be permanently pushed off.

steps.title: The plain reading does not make sense
steps.stepSummary: If the animals were set aside before the מזבח existed, they were pushed off from the very start, and that kind of pushing off is not permanent.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Was built'?! They were pushed off from the very beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the wording of the ברייתא. The words 'before it was built' cannot be what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals never had a usable מזבח at any point, so they were pushed off from the start (דחוי מעיקרא). That kind of pushing off does not disqualify them forever. A ruling of פסולין therefore does not fit this case, and the ברייתא must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushed off, put aside from being offered

steps.confusionAlert: Being pushed off 'from the start' is different from being fit and then pushed off. Only the second kind can make an animal permanently פסול.

phrases.english: 'Was built'?!
They are pushed off from the very beginning!
phrases.notes: He means these animals were never fit to be offered in the first place, so this is not the usual kind of permanent pushing off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ברייתא's wording can be read literally.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal wording of the ברייתא, 'before the altar was built'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being pushed off from the start is not a permanent disqualification, so 'פסולין' cannot be the ruling for this case.

steps.title: Second reading: before the מזבח was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא means animals set aside before the מזבח was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as 'before the altar was destroyed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new way of reading the ברייתא: the animals were set aside while the מזבח still stood, and then it was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading the animals were fit at first and were pushed off only later. That would be real pushing off, so the ruling of פסולין could make sense.

phrases.english: Rather, [read:] 'before the altar was destroyed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading of the ברייתא after the plain reading failed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about animals set aside before the מזבח existed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about animals set aside before the מזבח was destroyed.

steps.title: By then the animals would be too old
steps.stepSummary: If the מזבח was destroyed, by the time it is rebuilt the animals would be too old to offer.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Destroyed'?! By then they would have grown old!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second reading as well. If the whole מזבח was torn down, the animals would be too old by the time it was rebuilt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rebuilding a destroyed מזבח takes a very long time. The animals would be disqualified simply because of age, so the ברייתא would not need to teach anything about pushing off.

phrases.english: 'Destroyed'?!
But they have grown old!
phrases.notes: Sacrifices must be young animals, so old age by itself would already make them unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second proposed reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'before the altar was destroyed'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animals would become too old long before a rebuilt מזבח was ready, so the ruling would teach nothing about pushing off.

steps.title: Third reading: before the מזבח was damaged
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean animals set aside before the מזבח was damaged, and then it became damaged. Such animals are פסולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: before the altar was damaged, and afterward the altar was damaged, they are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on a reading that works: the מזבח was only damaged, not destroyed. Read this way, the ברייתא now seems to go against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A damaged מזבח can be repaired quickly, so age is not a problem. The animals were fit and then pushed off, and the ברייתא calls them פסולין. That sounds like even living animals are pushed off, which matches רבי יוחנן and goes against רב.

phrases.english: Rather, [read:] 'before the altar was damaged,'
'and afterward the altar was damaged, they are disqualified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final working reading, which brings the challenge against רב back into force.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a destroyed מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a damaged מזבח, and in that case it seems to disqualify even living animals.

steps.title: Since the text is being adjusted anyway, read 'that were slaughtered'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב: you are already adjusting the ברייתא, so adjust it to say the animals had already been slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But aren't you already adjusting the text? Then say: 'that were slaughtered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof against רב. Since we are already changing the wording, we can just as easily read it as talking about animals that were already slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב agrees that slaughtered animals are פסול when the מזבח becomes damaged. He only disagrees about living animals. If the ברייתא is about slaughtered animals, it says nothing against רב, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: You are fixing or adjusting the text

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא cannot prove that living animals are pushed off. It can be read as talking only about animals already slaughtered, which רב agrees are פסול.

phrases.english: But aren't you already adjusting [the text]?
Say: 'that were slaughtered.'
phrases.notes: So read the ברייתא as: animals that were slaughtered before the altar got damaged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא תָּרוֹצֵי קָא מְתָרְצַתְּ? אֵימָא: שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels the proof against רב that came out of the step 25 reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge from the ברייתא against רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's wording has to be adjusted anyway, so it can be adjusted to talk about slaughtered animals, a case where רב agrees.

steps.title: רב himself allows incense where the altar was uprooted
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: if the מזבח was uprooted, incense is still burned in its place. This suggests the מזבח is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב גידל say in the name of רב: if an altar was uprooted, we burn incense in its place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רב, this time using his own teaching. If incense can be burned with no altar there at all, why would a damaged מזבח disqualify sacrifices?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ruled that animals slaughtered while the מזבח was damaged are פסול, because the מזבח must be whole. Yet רב also says incense may be burned even when the altar is completely gone. These two rulings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Was uprooted, removed from its place

phrases.english: But didn't רב גידל say in the name of רב:
An altar that was uprooted:
phrases.notes: Since incense is burned on it, this is the inner golden altar.

phrases.english: we burn incense in its place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge against רב's basic ruling that a damaged מזבח disqualifies sacrifices.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that sacrifices slaughtered while the מזבח is damaged are פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If incense may be offered with no altar there at all, the altar seems unnecessary, so a damaged מזבח should not disqualify sacrifices.

steps.title: רב agrees that blood needs an altar
steps.stepSummary: Like רבא's statement that רבי יהודה agrees about blood, רב also agrees that placing the blood needs a real מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: רבי יהודה agreed about blood. Here too, רב agrees about blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 27. רב only allowed burning without a מזבח, but he agrees that blood must be placed on an actual מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 suggested that for רב the מזבח is not needed at all. The answer splits the cases: burning can be done in the place of the מזבח, but the blood needs the מזבח itself. So if the מזבח is damaged, the blood cannot be placed and the slaughtered animals are פסולין, just as רב ruled in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes (even though he usually holds differently)
Blood of the קרבן, which must be placed on the מזבח
Here too, the same applies in this case

phrases.english: As Rava said:
Rabbi Yehuda would concede regarding blood;
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה lets the whole courtyard be used for burning, but agrees that blood must go on the real מזבח.

phrases.english: here too, Rav concedes regarding blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב גידל's quote of רב in Step 27
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב holds that the מזבח is not needed for anything, so a damaged מזבח should not disqualify the animals
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds that burning does not need the מזבח, but blood does, so animals slaughtered when the מזבח is damaged are פסולין
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the blood service is tied to the physical מזבח in a way that burning is not.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה's view come from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source and context of רבי יהודה's view that was just mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just mentioned רבי יהודה, so it stops to ask what his view actually is. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side question, not an attack. The גמרא wants to show where the idea comes from that the courtyard can serve as a מזבח for burning.

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Yehuda's view?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the mention of רבי יהודה in the answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and content of רבי יהודה's position

steps.title: שלמה sanctified the courtyard because the altar was too small
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק literally. The מזבח was too small, so שלמה made the courtyard holy for offering. רבי יוסי begins to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: "On that day the king made holy the middle of the courtyard... because the altar was too small to hold." The words mean exactly what they say. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי said to him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind רבי יהודה's view. He reads the פסוק in מלכים literally, and then רבי יוסי starts to answer him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the מזבח really could not hold all of שלמה's קרבנות, so the courtyard floor was made holy and used for burning. This is where his idea comes from that the courtyard can serve for burning. רבי יוסי's reply continues in the next section.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש
The words are meant literally, just as written

steps.confusionAlert: The last line, "רבי יוסי said to him," is only the start of רבי יוסי's reply. What he actually says comes in the next section.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"On that day the king sanctified
the middle of the courtyard, etc.,
because the altar (that Moshe made)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The פסוק itself says "the copper altar that was before ה׳."

phrases.english: was too small to hold"
the words are as they are written.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei said to him,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא קִידַּשׁ הַמֶּלֶךְ תּוֹךְ הֶחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what רבי יהודה's view is
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה reads מלכים א 8:64 literally: the מזבח was too small, so the courtyard was made holy for burning
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the courtyard can serve for burning because שלמה made it holy when the מזבח was too small. Even so, he agrees that blood needs the real מזבח.
